title: LEI comparison uses Option<i64> PartialOrd with undocumented None semantics
description:
In events.rs lines 242-246, parse_state_counter returns Option<i64> and the comparison 'server_n <= lei_n' relies on Option<T>'s PartialOrd where None < Some(x) for all x.

If server_n is None (malformed state token from store) and lei_n is Some(n), then None <= Some(n) is true and replay is silently suppressed -- the server appears 'behind' when its state is unreadable. This is the wrong behavior: a malformed server state should trigger replay or a server error, not a silent no-op.

In practice, get_all_states() always returns well-formed 's-N' tokens (via format!("s-{counter}") from i64 database columns, or defaulting to 's-0'), so parse_state_counter never returns None for current_state. Similarly, the LEI header is validated at lines 161-171 to only accept 's-\d+' format, so parse_state_counter(lei) also never returns None. Both None arms are currently unreachable.

The risk is: the code is technically correct only because of two upstream invariants (store always produces s-N, header validation filters LEI). If either invariant is ever relaxed, the comparison silently misbehaves instead of failing loudly. A comment documenting the assumed invariants, or an explicit None match arm returning None (triggering replay on malformed state), would make the failure mode explicit.
